papers.title: ChAI-Net learns a regulatory code for chromatin co-accessibility.
papers.abstract: The regulation of chromatin accessibility is critical for cell function and identity. Advances in single-molecule long-read footprinting have enabled near-nucleotide-resolution readout of chromatin fiber organization, capturing both coordination of transcription factor (TF) binding and variation in nucleosome positioning previously obscured by bulk methods. Here we combine this technique with deep learning to study how protein-DNA interactions are coordinated within different types of cis -regulatory elements in mouse embryonic stem cells. First, we quantify the frequency with which pairs of p
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: ChAI-Net combines single-molecule long-read footprinting with deep learning to model how transcription factor binding and nucleosome positioning are coordinated within cis-regulatory elements in mouse embryonic stem cells. The work quantifies the frequency of paired protein-DNA interactions and learns a regulatory code governing chromatin co-accessibility at near-nucleotide resolution.

papers.title: Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney.
papers.abstract: Sequence-to-function (S2F) deep learning models predict genome-wide functional profiles directly from DNA sequences and have significantly advanced our understanding of gene regulation. However, existing S2F models are fundamentally constrained by their initial training datasets, and no single model encompasses the full spectrum of cell types, clinical conditions, and cellular states, while training new models de novo is nontrivial. Here, we develop Kidzoi, a kidney cell-type-specific S2F model obtained by transfer learning from the pretrained model Borzoi using single-nucleus chromatin access
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Kidzoi is a kidney cell-type-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model created by transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data. It enables prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects in a kidney-specific context, addressing the limitation that no single pretrained model covers all cell types and conditions. This approach demonstrates how transfer learning can efficiently adapt general genomic models to specialized tissues without training from scratch.

papers.title: A survival-informed CD8+ T cell-associated gene signature and its prognostic relevance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by marked clinical and immunological heterogeneity, and conventional clinicopathological variables do not fully capture patient survival risk. CD8+ T cells play a central role in antitumor immunity, yet their functional states can encompass both effective cytotoxic responses and dysfunctional immune programs. This study aimed to derive a survival-informed CD8+ T cell-associated gene signature and evaluate its prognostic associations, cellular expression, and relationship to immune dysfunction.
papers.summary: This study derived a survival-informed gene signature associated with CD8+ T cells in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and evaluated its prognostic value. The authors examined cellular expression patterns and the signature's relationship to immune dysfunction, aiming to improve risk stratification beyond conventional clinicopathological variables. The work highlights the dual functional states of CD8+ T cells—cytotoxic versus dysfunctional—in shaping ccRCC outcomes.

papers.title: Development and validation of a phase-stable computed tomography radiomics model for brain metastasis risk stratification in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Brain metastasis (BM) is a frequent complication of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but individualized risk stratification remains limited. We evaluated whether computed tomography (CT) radiomic features reproducible across non-enhanced and contrast-enhanced phases could improve BM risk prediction and whether integration with clinical biomarkers and semantic CT findings provided additional value.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates a CT radiomics model that uses features stable across non-enhanced and contrast-enhanced phases to stratify brain metastasis risk in NSCLC patients. It further tests whether combining radiomic features with clinical biomarkers and semantic CT findings improves predictive performance over radiomics alone.

papers.title: Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence contributes to tumor progression and shapes the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet its prognostic and biological significance in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA) remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify senescence-associated prognostic signals through pan-cancer screening and to develop an integrated risk stratification framework for BLCA that bridges molecular characterization with translational relevance.
papers.summary: This study identifies senescence-associated prognostic signals in bladder urothelial carcinoma by screening pan-cancer data and builds an integrated risk stratification model that links molecular features to the tumor microenvironment. The model aims to improve prognostication and connect molecular characterization with translational relevance for BLCA patients.

papers.title: From risk factors to individualized prediction: development and internal validation of a machine learning model for early identification of postoperative pneumonia after lung cancer surgery.
papers.abstract: Postoperative pneumonia (POP) remains one of the most common infectious complications following lung cancer surgery and is associated with substantial morbidity. Although several risk factors for POP have been identified, clinically applicable approaches for early individualized risk stratification remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine learning models for early prediction of POP using routinely available perioperative variables.
papers.summary: This study develops and internally validates machine learning models to predict postoperative pneumonia after lung cancer surgery using routinely available perioperative variables. The work aims to move beyond identifying general risk factors toward individualized early risk stratification, though validation is limited to an internal cohort.

papers.title: Species phylogenetics using intraprotein residue dependence inferred with protein foundation models.
papers.abstract: Traditional molecular phylogenetic inference uses multiple sequence alignments and amino acid substitution models that generally assume that sites evolve independently. In contrast, protein foundation models (pFMs) are deep learning models that reveal residue dependence patterns within sequences. There are two types of pFMs: Evolutionary Scale Models (esm-pFM) for analyzing individual protein sequences, and MSA Transformer (msat-pFM) models for analyzing MSAs. Using pFMs to analyze sequences produces residue attention matrices (RAMs) and sequence attention matrices (SAMs), respectively. RAMs a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint proposes using protein foundation models (pFMs) to infer phylogenetic relationships by capturing intraprotein residue dependencies, rather than relying on traditional alignment-based substitution models that assume site independence. The authors compare two pFM types—ESM models for individual sequences and MSA Transformer models for alignments—and derive residue attention matrices (RAMs) and sequence attention matrices (SAMs) as phylogenetic signals. The work suggests that deep-learning-derived attention patterns can provide an alternative or complementary source of evolutionary information for species phylogenetics.

papers.title: Attentive interpretable tabular learning (TabNet) for miRNA expression classification in cervical cancer and Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: The classification of RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data presents a fundamental challenge in computational biomedicine: raw read counts are high-dimensional, over-dispersed, and heteroscedastic, requiring careful preprocessing before machine learning models can be applied. Existing deep learning approaches for RNA-seq classification have largely overlooked the tabular nature of genomic expression data and have offered limited embedded interpretability. This study proposes TabNet, an attentive interpretable tabular learning architecture, as a framework for miRNA-based disease classification and eval
papers.summary: This study applies TabNet, an attention-based deep learning architecture designed for tabular data, to classify miRNA expression profiles from RNA-seq data for cervical cancer and Alzheimer's disease. The authors argue that RNA-seq data is inherently tabular and that TabNet's built-in interpretability makes it better suited than existing deep learning approaches. The work evaluates the framework on miRNA-based disease classification tasks.

papers.title: NeCS-Flow: Necrosis-Guided Contrast-Enhanced MRI Synthesis with Rectified-Flow Refinement.
papers.abstract: Gadolinium-based contrast agents raise concerns about tissue deposition, adverse reactions, and increased costs.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: NeCS-Flow presents a method to synthesize contrast-enhanced MRI from non-contrast scans using necrosis-guided information and rectified-flow refinement, aiming to reduce reliance on gadolinium-based contrast agents. The approach leverages necrosis cues to guide the synthesis and refines outputs with rectified flow, though the abstract provides limited detail on validation. This could help mitigate safety and cost concerns associated with contrast agents.

papers.title: Building from the ground up: augmentation strategies to improve protein language model performance on protein sets.
papers.abstract: An important underlying requirement for deep learning models is the availability of large datasets, however, in sciences such as chemistry and biology, generating experimental data of sufficient size represents a significant bottleneck. In this work, we probed the extent and nature of limited input data, characterize how several protein language models (pLMs) learned on suboptimal datasets, and investigated augmentation approaches to improve predictive model performance. We found that narrowing the distribution of protein-protein complexes in a limited dataset permits an order-ofmagnitude decr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors investigate how protein language models (pLMs) perform when trained on small, limited protein datasets, and test data augmentation strategies to improve predictive performance. They find that narrowing the distribution of protein-protein complexes in a limited dataset allows for an order-of-magnitude reduction in data requirements, suggesting targeted augmentation can compensate for data scarcity.

papers.title: AI-based prognosis and chemotherapy benefit in node-positive, HR+ breast cancer: a blinded external validation on SWOG-8814 trial.
papers.abstract: The benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy varies among patients with postmenopausal, node-positive, hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. Genomic assays identify patients likely to benefit from chemotherapy but are expensive and tissue consuming. AI-enabled biomarkers may provide scalable alternatives. We performed a blinded external evaluation of Ataraxis Breast CTX, a causal multi-modal AI model that integrates H&E images with clinical variables, in the phase III SWOG-8814 trial.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study externally validated an AI model (Ataraxis Breast CTX) that combines H&E histology images with clinical variables to predict prognosis and chemotherapy benefit in postmenopausal, node-positive, hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. Using a blinded evaluation on the SWOG-8814 phase III trial, the work tests whether an AI-based biomarker can serve as a scalable, tissue-sparing alternative to expensive genomic assays for guiding adjuvant chemotherapy decisions.

papers.title: Functional architecture of rare protein coding variation across 786,871 exomes.
papers.abstract: Protein coding variants span the gamut of structural and functional effects on proteins, and they have similarly heterogeneous effects on traits. Their functional effects can be predicted and categorized, particularly using machine learning models, and integrating these predictors benefits gene discovery. However, it remains unclear how well known structural features and predicted functional scores explain the heterogeneous effects of protein coding variants on human complex traits. We introduce the Kernel Allelic Series Model (KASM), which integrates multiple functional annotations to form a
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint introduces the Kernel Allelic Series Model (KASM), a method that integrates multiple functional annotations and machine learning-based predictors to model how rare protein-coding variants affect complex traits. Applied across 786,871 exomes, it shows that combining structural features and predicted functional scores better explains the heterogeneous effects of coding variants and improves gene discovery compared with single-annotation approaches.

papers.title: Predicting cell-state-specific gene regulation from DNA across species.
papers.abstract: DNA encodes the cell's phenotype, but the same DNA sequence is interpreted differently in every cell type, developmental stage, and activity state. Existing deep-learning models solve only half of this puzzle: sequence-to-function models read DNA but treat cell state as a fixed label, while single-cell foundation models represent cell state but not sequence. We developed Bolero, a sequence-to-function model whose parameters condition on atlas-scale cell-state embeddings and additional biological variables to predict cell-state-specific chromatin accessibility and transcript abundance from DNA.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present Bolero, a deep-learning model that predicts cell-state-specific chromatin accessibility and gene expression directly from DNA sequence. Unlike prior sequence-to-function models that treat cell state as a fixed label, Bolero conditions its parameters on atlas-scale single-cell embeddings and other biological variables, bridging sequence-based and cell-state-based modeling. This enables prediction of how the same DNA is interpreted differently across cell types, developmental stages, and activity states.

papers.title: De novo Design of a Vanadium Haloperoxidase.
papers.abstract: Organohalogens are an essential class of compounds for both synthetic chemistry and natural systems, yet the design of halogenases to catalyze carbon-halogen (C-X) bond formation has remained elusive. Vanadium-dependent haloperoxidases (V-HPOs) are attractive targets for such an effort, but they pose an unusual design problem: the vanadate (VO 4 3- ) cofactor is an anionic oxometalate that must be held by a precisely arranged network of hydrogen-bonding and electrostatic interactions rather than by the strong coordinate-covalent bonds through which proteins bind cationic transition metals. We
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint reports the de novo design of a protein that binds vanadate and functions as a vanadium-dependent haloperoxidase, an enzyme class that catalyzes carbon-halogen bond formation. The key challenge was that vanadate is an anionic oxometalate requiring a precise hydrogen-bonding and electrostatic network rather than the coordinate-covalent bonds used to bind typical cationic metals. Successfully designing such a cofactor-binding site demonstrates that de novo protein design can tackle unusual metallocofactor chemistries.

papers.title: Expanding the galactose oxidase substrate repertoire via a multi-modal computational strategy.
papers.abstract: Biocatalysis offers a greener alternative to chemical processes, yet industrial adoption is bottlenecked by the prohibitive cost of enzyme engineering. Here, we report a multi-modal computational framework that integrates synergistic descriptors of substrate binding, protein stability, and aggregation traits. Using galactose oxidase as a model system, this approach achieves 77% precision in identifying active variants across 13 structurally diverse secondary alcohols despite being trained exclusively on a single substrate. By implementing sequence conservation-based filtering, we demonstrate t
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that combines descriptors of substrate binding, protein stability, and aggregation to predict which engineered enzyme variants will be active. Using galactose oxidase as a test case, the method achieved 77% precision in identifying active variants for 13 structurally diverse secondary alcohols, even though it was trained on only a single substrate. Sequence conservation-based filtering further improved performance, suggesting a cost-effective route to broaden enzyme substrate scope.

papers.title: Explainable AI identifies recombination and chromatin environment as key predictors of subgenome evolution in maize and Brassica.
papers.abstract: Polyploidy, or whole genome duplication, reshapes genomes through biased gene loss and regulatory rewiring, yet the drivers of biased fractionation among subgenomes remain unclear. Using maize and Brassica rapa as model allopolyploids, we compiled 60 genomic and epigenomic features in maize and 45 in B. rapa and constructed supervised machine learning models to classify genes by subgenome identity. In both species, eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) approaches identified recombination rate as the most influential and highly interconnected feature despite nonsignificant mean differences
papers.summary: This study uses explainable machine learning on dozens of genomic and epigenomic features to predict which subgenome a gene belongs to in two allopolyploids, maize and Brassica rapa. Recombination rate emerged as the most influential and highly interconnected predictor of subgenome identity in both species, alongside chromatin environment, despite showing no significant mean differences between subgenomes. The work suggests biased fractionation after whole-genome duplication is driven by recombination and chromatin context rather than simple feature-level differences.

papers.title: kinGEMs: A robust and scalable framework for resource-constraint models through stochastic tuning of deep learning-predicted kinetic parameters.
papers.abstract: The construction of accurate enzyme-constrained genome-scale models (ecGEMs) remains a critical challenge in systems biology, limited by sparse kinetic data and the need for biologically meaningful representations. This work presents an integrated framework combining CPI-Pred, a deep learning model to predict kinetic parameters (kcat) from sequence and compound embeddings, with kinGEMs, a pipeline to incorporate these uncertainty-aware parameters into ecGEMs for metabolic optimization. By leveraging representations at multiple scales, the approach captures sequence, structure, and kinetic data
papers.summary: The authors present kinGEMs, a framework that combines a deep learning model (CPI-Pred) for predicting enzyme turnover numbers (kcat) from sequence and compound embeddings with a pipeline for incorporating these uncertainty-aware predictions into enzyme-constrained genome-scale metabolic models. This addresses the sparse kinetic data bottleneck in building ecGEMs by using stochastic tuning of predicted parameters to create resource-constraint models. The approach integrates sequence, structure, and kinetic information at multiple scales to improve metabolic optimization.

papers.title: Bridging generalizability and reproducibility in machine learning-based antimicrobial resistance prediction.
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of whole-genome sequencing and machine learning (ML) has led to a multitude of methods for predicting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) from bacterial genomic data. Despite increasingly high reported predictive performance, substantial differences in data sets, phenotype definitions, genomic preprocessing, evaluation strategies, and validation procedures make it difficult to determine whether models will perform reliably beyond the data on which they were developed. In machine learning, this problem is generally framed in terms of generalizability: the ability of a model to maint
papers.summary: This paper examines the challenges of generalizability and reproducibility in machine learning models that predict antimicrobial resistance from bacterial whole-genome sequencing data. It highlights how differences in datasets, phenotype definitions, genomic preprocessing, and validation strategies make it difficult to assess whether reported high performance will hold up on new data. The work likely proposes guidance or a framework for more standardized and reliable AMR prediction.

papers.title: TriTower-m6Am: A triple-tower heterogeneous deep learning architecture integrating semantic, sequential, and structural information for mRNA N6,2'-O-dimethyladenosine site prediction.
papers.abstract: N6,2'-O-dimethyladenosine (m6Am) is a cap-proximal mRNA modification deposited by PCIF1 (phosphorylated C-terminal domain (CTD)-interacting factor 1) at the first transcribed nucleotide of eukaryotic mRNAs. Knowing where m6Am sites sit would help explain how cells tune mRNA stability and translation, but current predictors typically depend on a single representation and do not jointly model multiple views of the same RNA sequence.
papers.summary: The paper introduces TriTower-m6Am, a deep learning model that predicts m6Am modification sites on mRNA by combining three complementary views of RNA sequence: semantic features, sequential patterns, and structural information. This triple-tower architecture aims to improve prediction accuracy over existing tools that rely on only one representation. The work addresses a gap in jointly modeling multiple data types for cap-proximal mRNA modification site identification.

papers.title: AOXP: An Integrated Framework for Antioxidant Peptide Prediction Leveraging LLM-Based Semantic Features and Optimized Physicochemical Ensembles.
papers.abstract: Oxidative stress is a critical driver of various severe diseases, positioning antioxidant peptides (APs) as promising therapeutic agents. However, their discovery is constrained by the limitations of low-throughput wet-lab assays and insufficient computational prediction tools. To address this, we developed Antioxidant Peptides eXplorer (AOXP), a deep learning framework that leverages multiscale feature integration for high-precision AP prediction. Unlike existing models that often rely on isolated sequence patterns or manual feature descriptors, AOXP employs a hybrid encoding strategy that sy
papers.summary: AOXP is a deep learning framework for predicting antioxidant peptides that combines LLM-derived semantic sequence features with optimized physicochemical descriptors in a hybrid encoding strategy. It aims to overcome the low throughput of wet-lab assays and the limited accuracy of prior computational tools by integrating multiscale features rather than relying on isolated sequence patterns or manual descriptors. The work positions itself as a high-precision predictor to accelerate discovery of antioxidant peptide therapeutics.

papers.title: Sequence-based coevolutionary prediction of species-specific interactomes.
papers.abstract: Evolutionarily conserved protein-protein interactions (PPIs) reveal fundamental biological processes. However, predicting protein function solely from these interactions provides an incomplete picture of biological systems. Computational methods for predicting PPIs often struggle due to limited functional annotations in databases, making it difficult to fully understand unique biological systems. This study introduces ContextMirror2.0 (CM2.0), a coevolution-based method designed to address these limitations. Coevolutionary approaches, unlike supervised machine learning methods, do not rely on
papers.summary: The authors present ContextMirror2.0 (CM2.0), a coevolution-based method for predicting species-specific protein-protein interactomes directly from sequence. Unlike supervised machine-learning approaches, it does not depend on existing functional annotations, allowing prediction of interactions in poorly annotated organisms. This addresses a key limitation in understanding unique biological systems where database coverage is sparse.

papers.title: Tumor-area mitosis proportion as an image-derived mitotic phenotype in lung squamous cell carcinoma: Patient-level prognostic and multi-omics evaluation.
papers.abstract: Mitotic activity is a recognized marker of tumor proliferation, yet its reproducible assessment across whole-slide images (WSIs) remains difficult. We developed a transfer-learning framework for lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) and evaluated whether a patch-derived tumor-area mitosis proportion (TAMP) was associated with survival and molecular tumor characteristics.
papers.summary: The authors developed a transfer-learning pipeline to quantify the proportion of tumor area containing mitotic figures (TAMP) from whole-slide images of lung squamous cell carcinoma. They then tested whether this image-derived mitotic phenotype was associated with patient survival and molecular features from multi-omics data. The work positions TAMP as a reproducible, computationally derived proliferation marker for LUSC.

papers.title: CT-Derived Body Composition Enhances Risk Prediction for Early Progression and Platinum Resistance in High-Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer.
papers.abstract: Patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) who develop resistance to platinum-based chemotherapy experience significantly poorer outcomes and shorter progression-free survival (PFS). This study evaluates whether pretreatment CT-based abdominal body composition is associated with platinum resistance and PFS, and whether its incorporation alongside clinical variables improves prognostic model performance.
papers.summary: This study examines whether body composition measurements derived from pre-treatment CT scans (such as abdominal fat and muscle) can predict platinum resistance and early progression in high-grade serous ovarian cancer. The authors test whether adding these imaging features to standard clinical variables improves prognostic model performance. The findings suggest CT-derived body composition may enhance risk stratification for this aggressive cancer.

papers.title: Identifying potential targets in endothelial to mesenchymal transition-mediated atherosclerosis using bioinformatics and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Endothelial to mesenchymal transition (EndMT) is a key driver of atherosclerosis (AS). This study integrated multiple RNA transcriptomic and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to identify shared gene expression signatures between EndMT and AS.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell RNA transcriptomic datasets to identify shared gene expression signatures between endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) and atherosclerosis. Using bioinformatics and machine learning, the authors pinpoint candidate genes that may serve as therapeutic targets for atherosclerosis. The work highlights the potential of EndMT-related signatures as biomarkers or intervention points.

papers.title: Development and temporal validation of an explainable machine learning model for predicting in-hospital diabetic foot ulcer in patients with type 2 diabetes using inflammatory-nutritional composite indices.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop and temporally validate explainable machine learning models for predicting in-hospital new-onset DFU in hospitalized patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) using routinely available admission variables and inflammatory-nutritional composite indices.
papers.summary: This study develops and temporally validates explainable machine learning models to predict new-onset diabetic foot ulcers during hospitalization in patients with type 2 diabetes, using routine admission variables and composite inflammatory-nutritional indices. The work emphasizes model interpretability and temporal validation, aiming to support early risk stratification in clinical settings.

papers.title: A deep learning model for automated assessment of neonates at risk of impaired breast crawl: a proof-of-concept video-based study.
papers.abstract: Timely initiation of breastfeeding is critical for newborn health. The breast crawl, an instinctive sequence of behaviors, is fundamental to this process. However, newborns vary considerably in their ability to complete the crawl, and current assessment relies on subjective endpoint observation. This approach cannot provide an early, objective measure of crawl competency or support timely intervention for at-risk mother-infant dyads.
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study proposes a deep learning model that analyzes videos of newborns to automatically assess their ability to perform the breast crawl, an instinctive behavior important for initiating breastfeeding. Current assessment relies on subjective observation of the endpoint, so the authors aim to provide an early, objective measure of crawl competency that could flag at-risk mother-infant dyads for timely intervention. The abstract describes the motivation and approach but does not report results.

papers.title: Multiparametric MRI-based radiomics combined with deep learning for preoperative risk stratification of endometrial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: To develop and compare radiomics, deep learning, clinical, and combined models based on multiparametric MRI radiomics and 2.5D deep learning features for preoperative risk stratification of endometrial carcinoma (EC).
papers.summary: This study develops and compares radiomics, deep learning, clinical, and combined models using multiparametric MRI to preoperatively stratify endometrial carcinoma risk. The combined approach integrating radiomics and 2.5D deep learning features is evaluated against individual models for risk classification. The work aims to improve preoperative risk assessment to guide clinical decision-making in endometrial cancer.

papers.title: Improving cognitive impairment classification in Alzheimer's disease using tabular diffusion augmentation and late fusion deep learning.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is the most common cause of dementia and is often detected after substantial neurodegeneration has occurred. Distinguishing cognitively impaired individuals from cognitively normal ones using genetic and demographic data can help characterize the genetic contributions to impairment. Deep learning can capture complex, nonlinear genetic relationships among these features, but its use in clinical genomics is limited by the small size of patient cohorts.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a method to improve classification of cognitive impairment in Alzheimer's disease by combining tabular diffusion-based data augmentation with late fusion deep learning, using genetic and demographic features. The approach addresses the challenge of small patient cohorts in clinical genomics, aiming to better capture nonlinear genetic relationships. The work is a methodological contribution to handling limited data in Alzheimer's genetic classification.

papers.title: Metallothionein-2A licenses an S100A8 alarmin program to drive epithelial-mesenchymal transition in pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a progressive interstitial lung disease driven in part by epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), but the upstream epithelial regulators remain undefined, and conventional screens rarely separate causal drivers from bystanders.
papers.summary: This study identifies metallothionein-2A (MT2A) as an upstream epithelial regulator that licenses an S100A8 alarmin program to promote epithelial-mesenchymal transition in pulmonary fibrosis. The work uses screening approaches designed to distinguish causal drivers from bystander genes, nominating MT2A as a driver of the EMT program relevant to PF pathogenesis.

papers.title: Integrative Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analyses Identify NFKBIE as a Candidate Gene Associated with IS-II Neutrophil Differentiation in Lung Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: People undergoing lung transplantation may develop lung ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI), in which neutrophils contribute to the inflammatory response. However, the molecular features associated with distinct neutrophil states remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify candidate molecular features associated with the immunosuppressive-II (IS-II) neutrophil state, with particular attention to NFKBIE, an NF-κB inhibitor.
papers.summary: This study combined bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to characterize neutrophil states in lung ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI), a complication of lung transplantation. The authors identified NFKBIE, an NF-κB inhibitor, as a candidate gene associated with the immunosuppressive-II (IS-II) neutrophil differentiation state. The work nominates a specific molecular marker for a functionally distinct neutrophil subset in LIRI.
